facts.text: Lilly, Georgia was founded in 1902 by brothers John, Frank, and Robert Lilly, who renamed the railroad town from Midway to honor themselves after discovering another Midway existed.
The Flint River borders the county’s west, its alluvial floodplain giving Lilly surrounding farmland its fertile soil.
Lilly was formally incorporated in 1907, adopting a unique circular city limit that wrapped around surrounding agricultural land.
A 1920 fire razed downtown, prompting a rebuild in brick and frame that showcases Greek Revival, Queen Anne, Folk Victorian, and Craftsman styles.
